A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same research work. Text, tables, figures, equations, and all appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A report original dialogue-generation experiments, numerical evaluations, and analyses varying persona count, polarity composition, and model size.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original human evaluations, persona-to-dialogue sentiment analysis, and results using GPT-4o as a dialogue generator.

M1.justification: v2 Section 4.2 adds an appended sentiment-aware instruction emphasizing negative and neutral persona integration while preserving coherence. This is a limited procedural addition to the retained turn-based generation and profile-ordering approach.

E1.justification: ConvAI2 dialogue generation and DialogNLI training of the evaluation model remain unchanged. Positive, negative, mixed, opposite, and neutral sentiment were already covered. The added neutral-profile grouping, human ratings, and GPT-4o experiments change configurations or evaluation within this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 retains the joint-generation, turn-based, and three ordering strategies from v1 Table 2. It adds sentiment-aware prompting alone as a comparator for the combined ordering-plus-prompting method, providing a limited expansion of the strategy comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces human evaluation using 40 randomly sampled Qwen persona-dialogue pairs per configuration, three English-speaking raters, and a 1–3 scale. Appendix A adds sentiment assessment using GPT-4o on a 1–5 scale, sampling 1,000 dialogues per model and constructing five-persona neutral profiles. Appendix C adds GPT-4o generation under the existing pairing protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix A investigates whether generated dialogues become more positive than their assigned personas. Section 4.3 separately evaluates sentiment-aware prompting and its combination with ordering. These add distinct mechanism and component analyses; the existing persona-count, polarity-ratio, and model-size analyses remain intact in Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run information, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 specifies human-rater counts and averaging as part of its new evaluation protocol but adds no uncertainty or inter-rater agreement estimates.

E6.justification: All matched earlier result entries remain unchanged. v2 adds prompting results, including combined-method C scores of 0.717 for LLaMa-3.2 and 0.774 for Qwen-2.5 in Table 3. The new human comparison reports consistency of 1.80 versus 2.27 and coherence of 2.40 versus 2.43 (Table 4). Tables 2, 5, and 6 additionally report human polarity comparisons, sentiment shifts, and GPT-4o generation results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of C score, contradiction ratio, and dialogue-level coherence are unchanged from v1 Appendix B to v2 Appendix D. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the proposed contribution to include sentiment-aware prompting alongside turn-based generation and profile ordering. The central findings about persona sentiment sensitivity remain the same, and the conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix A attributes sensitivity to scarce negative pretraining material and positivity encouraged by post-training. Section 4.3 adds a decoding-based explanation for ordering/prompting synergy, while Appendix C discusses downstream implications of GPT-4o sensitivity. These substantially extend the interpretation, although the training-related causes are not experimentally isolated. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link and states that the implementation is publicly available. Section 4.2 supplies the new sentiment instruction's exact wording and placement. Existing hardware, decoding limits, evaluation-model training details, and original prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work sections are unchanged. The paper retains its positioning around sentiment embedded in explicit personas, personalized dialogue generation, and dialogue evaluation.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract, introduction, and acknowledgment edits, expands the evaluation and method discussion, and inserts two appendices. The main section sequence and much of the existing prose remain unchanged; retained appendices are renumbered.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact tables and expands the generation-strategy table with prompting rows and an updated caption. Existing figure artwork, plots, and prompt diagrams are retained. Figures and text reflow within the same two-column format, and printed page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens v1's automated-only evidence with human ratings supporting positive pairings and the combined method's consistency benefit. Component comparisons, GPT-4o results, and implementation access information also improve validation and reproducibility. The net gain is limited: human evaluation uses 40 samples per configuration without uncertainty estimates, its coherence gain is only 0.03, and the new training-related causal explanations remain untested.
